# A Gantt's tree-column sort: the header never sorts, links stay behind

No curated label: owned work from the operator's 20 Nov read of the home page, due before the Engine 14 examples lock (Sun 22 Nov 17:00Z).

## Context

@tobiu reported on 2026-11-20 that the home plan preview's Gantt "breaks every dependency link after a tree-column sort" and needs proper tree-column support. A first headless check (three Task-header clicks) found the links on their bars and called it not reproduced. That check measured nothing: the header click never sorted the store, so no row moved.

Measured headless on `dev` `2c1d8e8c86` (Chrome, 1440 × 900, `#/home`, the "Gantt & Task Board" page):

| Step | Task header | Plan store `sortProperties` | Rows, top to bottom | Links off their bars |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| at rest | `neo-sort-hidden` | `[]` | Design, Wireframes, Visual design, Prototype, Build, … | 0 of 8 |
| header click | `neo-sort-asc`, `aria-sort="ascending"` | `[]` | unchanged | 0 of 8 |
| second click | `neo-sort-desc`, `aria-sort="descending"` | `[]` | unchanged | 0 of 8 |
| `Gantt#onSortColumn({property: 'title', direction: 'ASC'})` | — | `['title']` | Build, Data layer, Grid views, Scheduling, Design, Prototype, Visual design, Wireframes, Launch, Go live, Load test | 4 of 8, up to 156 px (three 52 px rows) |

The last row is the operator's frame: the bars move with their rows, every arrow stays where its rows used to be. The store itself is right: a unit run of `Neo.gantt.TaskStore` with the preview's eleven tasks sorts the tree by `title` ASC and DESC and fires `sort` once per call.

## The Problem

Two defects stack, and either one alone breaks the tree column of every Gantt:

1. **The header's sort never reaches the store.** The button flips its arrow and `aria-sort`, so the chart says it is sorted while it is not.
2. **A sort leaves the dependency overlay behind.** Once the store is sorted by any path, the rows move and the links stay on the old rows.

The first defect is not the Gantt's own: every `Neo.grid.Container` subclass with an ntype of its own (`scheduler`, `gantt`) loses the header's sort, its inline header filter and its column menu's store binding the same way.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/header/Button.mjs` `afterSetIsSorted()` resolves its grid with `me.up('grid-container')` and returns before `fire('sort')` when that finds nothing. `ComponentManager.up()` turns a string into `{ntype: 'grid-container'}`, an exact match, so a header inside `Neo.scheduler.Container` (`ntype: 'scheduler'`) or `Neo.gantt.Container` (`ntype: 'gantt'`) finds no grid. The same lookup feeds `afterSetDataField()`, `changeFilterOperator()` and `changeFilterValue()` in that file, `src/grid/header/plugin/Menu.mjs` (the menu's store binding) and `src/plugin/HeaderFilter.mjs`.
- The header toolbar already holds the reference: `src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs` has a `gridContainer` config and reads it for its bodies.
- `src/grid/Container.mjs` `createColumns()` wires `onSortColumn` as every column header's `sort` listener; `Neo.scheduler.Container#createColumns()` builds its locked and timeline columns and passes them through it, so the listener is in place and never called.
- `src/gantt/Container.mjs` `afterSetStore()` re-projects the dependency layer on the task store's `mutate`, `recordChange`, `rowsChange` and `filter`. `sort` is not in that list.

Design authority: "A store batch (`updateRows()`) re-projects the overlay once, on its `rowsChange`. Its records' `recordChange` events and the filter or sort it reapplies arrive first, while `store.isUpdatingRows` is true, and leave the overlay to that final event." (`Neo.gantt.Container#afterSetStore` JSDoc: the overlay follows a sort, and only a batch defers it.) And `Neo.data.TreeStore#doSort`: "Hierarchically sorts the TreeStore."

## The Fix

1. **One grid lookup for the header family.** `grid/header/Button` resolves its grid through its header toolbar's `gridContainer`, the reference the grid container sets on its own toolbars, before any ntype match. Every reader listed above uses that one resolution. A grid subclass keeps its own ntype. The ntype match stays only as the fallback for a header placed under a bare `grid-container`, and for `plugin/HeaderFilter`'s other owners: its contract follows any header "without adding a source ownership API".
2. **The overlay follows a sort.** `Neo.gantt.Container#afterSetStore()` adds `sort` to the task-store listeners. A sort changes no date, so it re-projects the dependency layer without invalidating the schedule, and a sort inside an `updateRows()` batch still defers to its `rowsChange`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: In the home plan preview, a Task-header click sorts the plan store by `title` (rows ASC within their phase), a second click sorts DESC, and the header's arrow and `aria-sort` match the store.
- [ ] AC-2: After each of those sorts, every dependency link starts at its predecessor bar and ends at its successor bar within 1 px. An e2e asserts AC-1 and AC-2; it is red on `dev` and green at the head.
- [ ] AC-3: A `Neo.scheduler.Container` resource-column header click sorts its resource store (unit or e2e).
- [ ] AC-4: The header's inline filter and its column menu bind to the store of a grid subclass with its own ntype (unit test on a Gantt or Scheduler).
- [ ] AC-5: Every grid lookup in `src/grid/header/` and `src/plugin/HeaderFilter.mjs` asks the header's toolbar first (`Button#getGridContainer()`); `up('grid-container')` remains only as that fallback.

## Out of Scope

- Which records a tree sort moves: `TreeStore#doSort` sorts siblings within their parent, and that contract stands.
- The board's card order: the board reads its own `order` field, not the grid's sorters.
- The cascade motion of an open pull request (#21648): a sort is not a cascade and takes no transition.

## Avoided Traps

- **Matching more ntypes** (`up('grid-container') || up('scheduler') || up('gantt')`): every next subclass repeats the defect. The toolbar's reference is the grid that built the header.
- **Re-syncing the overlay from the grid body's row render:** the overlay already follows the store everywhere else; a second trigger in the view is a second clock.
